title: Trump: Miss Teen USA: Donald gets lap dance from Ivanka, watches girls undress
description_short: Trump: Miss Teen USA: Donald gets lap dance from Ivanka, watches girls undress
description_medium: TrumpFile.org’s timeline alleges that Donald Trump asked his daughter Ivanka for a lap dance during rehearsals for the 1997 Miss Teen USA pageant, when it says she was 15. The same page attributes additional claims about contestants to former Apprentice staffer Noel Casler. The supplied source does not provide a direct Casler statement or corroborating records.
notes: The linked page was read and contains serious allegations attributed to Noel Casler and unnamed contestants, but no direct quotation from Casler, contemporaneous pageant records or response from the people named. The claim that Ivanka was 15 and the specific rehearsal chronology also require corroboration.
proposed_correction: Keep the claims explicitly attributed, verify Ivanka’s age and the event chronology, and add a direct or corroborating source before treating the alleged conduct as established.

title: Reproductive Health Data Privacy Elimination - Federal Surveillance and Tracking System
description_short: Reproductive Health Data Privacy Elimination - Federal Surveillance and Tracking System
description_medium: A Guttmacher Institute fact sheet described Project 2025 recommendations for states to report abortions, miscarriages and stillbirths to the federal government. The organization warned that collection of reproductive-health information could expose patients and providers to surveillance or misuse. The analysis describes a proposed policy and potential risks, not an implemented federal tracking system.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented Project 2025's comprehensive elimination of reproductive health data privacy by mandating federal reporting of all abortions, miscarriages, and stillbirths while creating surveillance systems that tracked women's reproductive choices and enabled prosecution of abortion providers and patients through weaponized data collection. The systematic privacy destruction represented Trump's implementation of 'pregnancy and abortion surveillance at the federal level' that eliminated medical confidentiality while forcing healthcare providers to report private reproductive information to government agencies that used the data for criminal investigations and prosecutions. The reproductive surveillance included requiring states to provide comprehensive abortion data to federal authorities under threat of losing funding streams, while creating databases that tracked individual women's reproductive outcomes and enabled cross-referencing with other government data to identify and prosecute those who sought or provided abortion care. Trump's data weaponization violated medical privacy protections by eliminating patient confidentiality while creating government surveillance systems that monitored reproductive choices, effectively transforming private medical decisions into criminal intelligence gathering operations that targeted women and healthcare providers. The reproductive tracking system created what advocates called 'immediate threat to abortion providers and patients' through data collection that enabled 'increased criminalization of pregnancy outcomes' while providing authorities with comprehensive records for prosecuting reproductive healthcare as criminal activity. The privacy elimination represented Project 2025's vision of reproductive surveillance as law enforcement tool rather than medical privacy protection, transforming healthcare data from confidential patient information into government surveillance records that enabled systematic persecution of reproductive autonomy and medical decision-making through comprehensive tracking and criminalization of pregnancy outcomes.
subcategory: Reproductive Privacy Surveillance and Medical Data Weaponization
notes: Guttmacher’s October 2024 analysis concerns Project 2025 recommendations and possible misuse. The other linked material does not document a CDC directive, required data fields, funding conditions imposed on states or an implemented tracking system, all of which the preserved long description asserts.
proposed_correction: Revise the existing long description to describe the proposal and attributed risk assessment, removing claims of a federal mandate, actual surveillance system or prosecutions unless supported by implementation records.

title: Child Tax Credit and EITC Elimination - $120 Billion Anti-Poverty Program Termination
description_short: Child Tax Credit and EITC Elimination - $120 Billion Anti-Poverty Program Termination
description_medium: An August 2024 Joint Economic Committee analysis said Project 2025 proposed removing most deductions, credits and exclusions without specifically preserving the Child Tax Credit or Earned Income Tax Credit. It estimated that a family of four earning $90,000 would pay about $6,300 more if the Child Tax Credit were also eliminated; the figure modeled a proposal, not an enacted change.
description_long: Donald Trump eliminated the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit by implementing Project 2025's plan to remove 'most tax credits, deductions, and exclusions' while raising taxes on middle-class families by $6,300 annually to fund tax cuts for millionaires through systematic destruction of America's largest anti-poverty programs. The comprehensive tax credit elimination represented Trump's abandonment of 23 million Americans who would fall deeper into poverty through EITC termination, while eliminating CTC benefits that had lifted 4.3 million people out of poverty including 2.3 million children in 2018 alone. The anti-poverty program destruction included ending refundable tax credits that provided essential income support to working families earning at least $2,500 annually, while simultaneously reducing tax rates for wealthy Americans from 32-37% to 30% maximum rate that benefited households with income over $383,900. Trump's tax elimination violated federal anti-poverty obligations by removing income support that had historically reduced child poverty while forcing working families to pay higher taxes to subsidize millionaire tax cuts, effectively transferring wealth from low-income families to wealthy individuals through regressive tax restructuring. The credit termination created what policy experts called systematic abandonment of working families through elimination of tax policy that had provided economic security while reducing inequality, transforming federal tax system from poverty reduction tool into mechanism that increased hardship for vulnerable families while enriching the wealthy. The anti-poverty program elimination represented Project 2025's vision of tax policy that prioritized wealth concentration over poverty reduction, systematically removing support for working families while providing massive tax benefits to millionaires through regressive restructuring that increased inequality and economic hardship for America's most vulnerable children and families.
subcategory: Anti-Poverty Program Elimination and Regressive Tax Policy
notes: The Joint Economic Committee and other linked sources discuss Project 2025 tax proposals and modeled effects. They do not establish that Trump eliminated the Child Tax Credit or EITC, as the preserved long description claims.
proposed_correction: Revise the existing long description to distinguish the proposal from enacted law, retain tax-impact figures only with their assumptions and source, and remove the claim that the credits were terminated.

title: Donald Trump announces Trump SoHo, developed by criminals Sater & Arif
description_short: Donald Trump announces Trump SoHo, developed by criminals Sater & Arif
description_medium: On an episode of The Apprentice in 2006, Donald Trump announced the Trump SoHo condominium project, a partnership involving the Trump Organization, the Sapir Organization and Bayrock Group. The linked New York Times report described Bayrock’s role and Feliks Sater’s prior racketeering plea; it did not establish criminal conduct by the Trump Organization or every developer named in the title.
notes: The New York Times link returned HTTP 403. The supplied source notes say it documents Bayrock’s partnership, Sater’s 1998 racketeering plea and a Manhattan investigation that closed without charges. They also say Trump denied knowing Sater well. The sources do not establish criminal conduct by the Trump Organization or Tamir Arif.
proposed_correction: Retain the project announcement and documented partnership, but remove “developed by criminals” unless each person’s role and relevant criminal finding are specified and sourced.

title: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
description_short: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
description_medium: TrumpFile.org’s timeline says roughly 1,000 people gathered in St. Louis in February 2009 to protest the economic crash and Barack Obama’s election. It describes Tea Party organizations as a network involving Americans for Prosperity and other conservative groups and links that network to Koch funding. The supplied source does not show a complete grant record or a specific takeover of Republican leadership.
notes: The linked timeline and reporting support Koch backing for Americans for Prosperity and its role in conservative campaigns, but do not provide a full grant ledger or prove that the February gathering was directed by the Koch brothers or aimed at taking control of the Republican Party.
proposed_correction: Specify the organizations and documented funding relationship, attribute the “take over” language to its source, and avoid asserting a direct funding or control relationship without a grant or coordination record.

title: Trump: ‘Something awoke' in J.D. Vance after meeting Peter Thiel
description_short: Trump: ‘Something awoke' in J.D. Vance after meeting Peter Thiel
description_medium: At Yale Law School in 2011, J.D. Vance attended a speech by investor Peter Thiel and later wrote that it reshaped how he thought about achievement and professional ambition. Vance called the talk the most significant moment of his time at Yale in a 2020 reflection. The timeline says the two later became friends and collaborators.
notes: The linked timeline provides Vance’s retrospective account of a formative speech and their later friendship. It does not supply enough detail about the speech or the meeting to support a distinct 140-word event explanation, and the influence claim should not be generalized into proof of Vance’s later political motives.
proposed_correction: Add the full Vance reflection and the speech’s specific content, while keeping the influence claim attributed to Vance and avoiding unsupported claims about later motives.

title: Trump: The Obama administration cuts funding for Soviet Union research
description_short: Trump: The Obama administration cuts funding for Soviet Union research
description_medium: The Obama administration cuts funding for Soviet Union research. The Obama administration begins to cut funding for research on the former Soviet Union (and therefore Russia). This continues into 2015 as resources are shifted to confront Syria, ISIS, and gun violence. This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, legal development, documented relationship, or policy consequence linked directly or indirectly to Trump. The downstream effects include institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and accountability pressure across affected systems.
notes: The supplied timeline says the Obama administration reduced funding for research on the former Soviet Union during 2014–15, but gives no amounts, affected programs or institutions, or evidence for the stated reason. The event predates Trump and the input does not establish a meaningful connection to him.
proposed_correction: Provide the budget line, affected programs and decision documents, or remove this item from the Trump-focused event collection.

title: Criminal Penalties for Trans Students and Families - Prosecution of Gender-Affirming Support
description_short: Criminal Penalties for Trans Students and Families - Prosecution of Gender-Affirming Support
description_long: Donald Trump implemented systematic criminalization of transgender students and their families by prosecuting parents who provided gender-affirming support while classifying teachers, librarians, and healthcare providers as 'sexual predators' and 'pornographers' for acknowledging transgender existence through Project 2025's comprehensive targeting of transgender youth and supportive communities. The comprehensive family criminalization represented Trump's expansion of anti-transgender persecution to include prosecution of parents for supporting their children's gender identity while requiring schools to refer students by birth certificate names unless parents provided written permission that could trigger Child Protective Services investigations. The transgender targeting included prosecuting families for allowing their children to use bathrooms consistent with gender identity while criminalizing public displays of transgender identity through laws that classified gender expression as 'sexual predation' subject to arrest and registration as sex offender. Trump's family persecution violated constitutional protections for parental rights and family autonomy by criminalizing supportive parenting while using state power to separate transgender youth from affirming families through child welfare investigations that prioritized conservative ideology over child welfare and family unity. The criminal prosecution system created what advocates called 'systematic family destruction' through legal mechanisms that punished transgender youth and their supporters while forcing families to choose between affirming their children's identity or avoiding criminal prosecution and child removal by state authorities. The transgender criminalization represented Project 2025's vision of family control based on conservative gender ideology rather than parental autonomy, transforming supportive parenting from protected family relationship into criminal activity while using state power to enforce gender conformity through prosecution and family separation rather than child welfare and family preservation.
subcategory: Transgender Family Criminalization and Child Persecution
notes: The linked NWLC, PEN America and NEA materials describe Project 2025 proposals and state education policies, not a federal statute or documented prosecution of families for supporting transgender youth. The supplied sources do not identify a federal charge or child-welfare case matching the title and preserved long description.
proposed_correction: Identify the specific law, case or federal action and its date; otherwise describe the cited proposals as proposals and remove claims of completed prosecution or criminal penalties.

title: Trump: Roger Stone allegedly has dinner with Julian Assange, starts covering for Russia
description_short: Trump: Roger Stone allegedly has dinner with Julian Assange, starts covering for Russia
notes: The linked timeline describes the dinner as alleged and questions whether Stone and Assange could have met, noting Stone was in Los Angeles for much of the evening and Assange would have needed to enter the country. It supplies no independent confirmation of a physical meeting or evidence connecting it to a change in Stone’s statements about the DNC hack.
proposed_correction: Verify whether a meeting occurred and provide a reliable source for the date and location before describing it as an event or claiming it caused Stone to cover for Russia.

title: Trump: Jared Kushner meets with Putin-appointed Russian banker
description_short: Trump: Jared Kushner meets with Putin-appointed Russian banker
description_medium: On December 13, 2016, Jared Kushner met with Sergei Gorkov, head of Russia’s state-owned Vnesheconombank, after Russian Ambassador Sergey Kislyak arranged the meeting. Accounts differed about whether it concerned Trump’s transition, real estate or a diplomatic favor. Kushner later said Gorkov gave him two gifts from Belarus.
description_long: On December 13, 2016, Jared Kushner met with Sergei Gorkov, the chief executive of Russia’s state-owned Vnesheconombank, in a meeting arranged by Russian Ambassador Sergey Kislyak. The encounter came about two weeks after Kushner and Kislyak discussed a possible private communication channel between the Trump transition team and Moscow. Kushner was also seeking investors for a Manhattan office building connected to Anbang Insurance Group. Accounts of the meeting’s purpose differed: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov described it as ordinary real-estate business; the White House said it was transition-related; Kushner later called it a favor to Kislyak. Kushner said Gorkov discussed his bank and the Russian economy and gave him a bag of soil and a piece of art from Belarus, where Kushner’s grandparents were from. These competing explanations made the meeting a subject of scrutiny, but do not by themselves establish secret diplomacy or a business deal.
